header.subject: English
header.chapter: Ch.4 Pinky and Jojo's TV Troubles!
header.title: Siblings & Sharing: key words + picture match
header.goal: Children say and use share, pull and tug-of-war.

bring: textbook p.39 · chalk · dupatta (the rope) · books, pencils

moves.do: Ask three quick recall questions; the class answers together.
moves.how: Names start with a …? What helps us see?
moves.say: “What do we wash before we eat?” → “Hands.”

moves.do: Open p.39: point to title, Pinky's face, word box.
moves.how: Class: “I see …”. Ask: “Who do you share with at home?”
moves.say: “Today: share, pull, tug-of-war. The word box is our dictionary.”

moves.do: Model SAY, FIND, ACT, USE on “share”, then “pull”.
moves.how: Box meaning. Share: a pencil. Pull: a door.
moves.say: “Zainab shared her pencil. Pull brings it to me.”
moves.think: I need the meaning, so I look in the word box, I do not guess. It says letting others use what I have. So Zainab shared.

moves.do: Run a gentle dupatta pull; class says tug – of – war in three parts.
moves.how: Read the box meaning; class finishes it.
moves.say: “Each team pulls. Sports day: we play …” → “… tug-of-war!”

moves.do: Tell a home scene; neighbour shows 1, 2 or 3 fingers. One minute.
moves.how: Zainab and Bilal show it first. One tells a home scene; other shows 1 finger share, 2 pull, 3 tug-of-war; check the box.
moves.say: “Tell a home scene. Show 1, 2 or 3 fingers.”

turn.a: I give my sister half my roti.
turn.help: Act the word: pass an eraser; say “share”.

moves.do: Match the three words to pictures alone, p.39 Exercise 1.
moves.how: 1. share · 2. pull · 3. tug-of-war. Done? Write one sentence.
moves.say: “Who shares one thing? What moves towards someone?”

answers: middle: a ball offered to a child
sections.mistake: Matches by first letter. Ask: “Who uses one thing together?”
sections.stuck: Act the word: you say “share”, they pass an eraser.

moves.do: Say a scene: “Ayesha lets her cousin ride her new bicycle.”
moves.how: Five say the word, then a sentence with pull or tug-of-war.

sections.correct: “share”, and an own sentence with “pull” or “tug-of-war” used correctly.
sections.success: I can say and use share, pull and tug-of-war.
sections.ask: How do you know Ayesha's bicycle is share?
sections.listen: She lets her cousin use it: share means letting others use what you have.

moves.do: Ask your family Pinky's questions about brothers and sisters.
moves.how: Draw one thing you shared; write “share” under it.
